To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The forced infiltration system with one subsurface drain parallel with the surface slope was more effective at removing pollutants from runoff water from a feedlot than the two consecutive 30m filter strips.

The subsurface drain system with a single drain parallel to the slope discharged less of most of the pollutants than the sodded filter strips, but the other system with cross slope subsurface drainage and surface dikes performed similarly to the first 30 m of sodded filter strip and less than the second 30 m of filter strip.

the forced infiltration system was more effective in reducing runoff volume, total nitrogen, ammonium nitrogen and soluble phosphorus than the sodded filter strips but less effective in reducing chemical oxygen demand, nitrate nitrogen and organic nitrogen than the filter strips.
